13.meaning: A verb meaning 'We enjoined, charged, or solemnly instructed' — to give a binding directive or earnest counsel, often as a charge laid upon someone. The intensive pattern conveys emphatic, weighty instruction.
13.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern ('to charge emphatically'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we.' The action is presented as already accomplished.

14.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

15.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
15.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

16.meaning: 'And Moses (Mūsā)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
16.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It ends in a fixed long '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) and so shows no visible change for case.

17.meaning: And ʿĪsā (Jesus) — the proper name of the Messenger ʿĪsā son of Maryam, upon him be peace, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
17.grammar: Wa- is the connector 'and'. ʿĪsā is a foreign-origin proper name ending in the fixed -ā sound: names like this do not change their ending for case at all, so the same form serves whatever role the name plays.

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

19.meaning: 'Establish! / set up firmly / keep up' (addressed to more than one person) — a command to make something stand upright, perform it properly, and maintain it steadfastly. The root revolves around standing and uprightness.

parts.en: verbal stem: establish / set up / keep up

19.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in the causative (afʿala) pattern, meaning to make something stand / establish it. The -ū ending directs the command to a masculine plural audience — 'you all, establish!' This pattern carries the active sense of setting something up and keeping it firmly in place.
19.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; uprightness, establishing

20.meaning: The dīn — a deep term covering religion, the way of life, the path of obedience and worship owed to Allah, and the reckoning/recompense for it; a complete system of belief and practice with accountability.
20.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles.

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

22.meaning: You (all) become divided / split into factions — Form V tafarraqa pictures a group breaking itself apart into separate camps, the opposite of holding together as one.
22.grammar: The first ta- marks 'you' in the imperfect (present) tense; the plural -ū says the doers are a group. Crucially, the ending is bare -ū with no final -na: dropping that -na is how Arabic marks this verb form as governed by a particle before it — typically 'do not…' (prohibition) or 'that…' (purpose) — rather than a plain statement, which would be tatafarraqūna.

23.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
23.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

24.meaning: A finite past-tense verb meaning 'it became great/weighty/burdensome' — that something grew large, heavy, hard to bear, or oppressive to the heart. Often used of a matter felt as overwhelming or intolerably difficult.
24.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The intransitive vowel pattern (-u- in the middle) indicates an inherent quality — it 'is/became' great rather than acting on something. The final -a is the standard ending of this past-tense form.

25.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
25.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
25.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

26.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
26.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

27.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
27.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

28.meaning: 'You call them / you invoke them' — a present-tense verb. From the root for calling, it covers summoning, appealing to, or invoking someone (as in calling upon a deity). The attached pronoun is the object, 'them.'
28.grammar: A present-tense action with a 'you' (masculine) subject built into the ta- prefix. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). The verb commonly carries the sense of calling upon or invoking.
28.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

29.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
29.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

30.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
30.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

31.meaning: He chooses / selects for Himself — ijtabā is to pick something out and draw it to oneself; used of Allah electing whom He wills for His guidance and service.
31.grammar: The ya- prefix marks the imperfect (present/ongoing) tense with 'He' as the doer. The verb is Form VIII (ijtabā), whose inserted -t- gives the nuance 'for oneself': He draws His chosen one to Himself. The final -ī is the weak last root letter surfacing as a long vowel; for such verbs this -ī form is the ordinary indicative (plain statement) form.

32.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
32.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

33.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
33.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

34.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
34.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
34.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

35.meaning: 'And he/it guides, leads rightly, directs to the way' — a verb for showing the right path and leading someone toward correct guidance.
35.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb from a weak-final root, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the masculine singular subject and the stem ends in a long ī; the prefixed wa- means 'and'.
35.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, leading to the right way

36.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
36.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

37.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
37.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

38.meaning: 'He turns (in repentance) / returns'. The form-IV verb anāba means to turn back to Allah repeatedly in penitence and devotion, a recurring orientation of the heart toward Him.

parts.en: turn back / return penitently (form IV stem)

38.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) active verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'). The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood for a verb making a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action (not commanded, negated, or made conditional). The form-IV pattern adds the nuance of turning toward / devoting oneself.
38.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to turn, return; (form IV) to turn to (Allah) in repentance

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: They became divided / split into sects — the completed act of a community breaking apart into rival factions.
2.grammar: A perfect (completed-action) verb in Form V, the pattern of undergoing a splitting — 'they broke into factions'. The -ū ending is the past-tense marker for 'they (a group of people)'; the silent alif written after it is purely a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
5.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: It came to them / he came to them: a completed act of arriving or coming, with the recipients ('them') built into the word.

parts.en: final vowel of the past-tense base (he/it)

7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), expressing a completed action. In this form the 'he/it' subject carries no added suffix — the -a is simply the final vowel resting on the last root letter of the base, not a person marker. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.
7.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

8.meaning: Knowledge: sure, certain knowing — grasping a thing as it truly is. As a verbal noun it names the state or body of knowledge itself.
8.grammar: A definite noun with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being named.

9.meaning: A noun in the accusative meaning 'out of envy / resentment / wrongful insolence' — overstepping due bounds, often from jealousy of what others have been given. It commonly functions adverbially to give the motive 'because of envy.'
9.grammar: The -an ending (indefinite accusative, called tanwīn) often marks a word as the reason or manner of an action — answering 'why?' or 'how?' Here it conveys 'out of / because of' the named quality.
9.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — exceeding proper limits; envy, insolence, wrongful desire

10.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
10.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

11.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

11.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

12.meaning: 'A word / an utterance / a statement' — a single unit of speech; by extension a decree, pronouncement, or settled saying.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation: nominative is the form typically used for the subject of a sentence, and the -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a word'). The feminine -t (tā' marbūṭa) is sounded here because the case ending follows it.

13.meaning: 'It preceded / went before / came earlier' — a (feminine) thing that came first or was already established beforehand.
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -at ending (here -t with a silent stop) marks the third-person feminine singular ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine subject, and indicates a completed action ('it has gone before').
13.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, go ahead, outstrip

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
15.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

16.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
16.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

17.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
17.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
17.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

18.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
18.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
18.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

19.meaning: 'It would surely have been decreed / settled / brought to an end.' The verb is the passive of qaḍā ('to decide, decree, conclude'), prefixed by an emphatic 'la-' meaning 'surely/certainly,' often answering a condition.
19.grammar: A passive past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it was decreed/concluded'); the passive is shown by the internal vowel pattern qu-i-a, and the bare -a ending carries no named agent. The prefixed la- is an emphatic particle ('surely'), commonly introducing the answer to a conditional.
19.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decide, decree, judge, bring to completion

20.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
20.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
20.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

21.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
21.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

22.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
22.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

23.meaning: They were made to inherit — to receive something passed down from those before, here in the passive: inheritance was handed to them rather than earned; in the Qur'an often said of receiving the Scripture from earlier generations.
23.grammar: This is Form IV awratha ('to cause to inherit') turned passive: the ū- vowelling at the start is the classic passive marking, so the doers received the action — 'they WERE made to inherit'. The -ū ending marks 'they (a group)' as the ones affected, in the past tense.

24.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
24.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
24.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
26.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).

27.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'surely in / indeed within'. It joins an emphasis particle ('surely, indeed') with the preposition 'in', stressing that something is firmly located or contained inside.
27.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, indeed') used to strengthen a statement. fī is a preposition ('in/within') and, like all prepositions, governs a following noun, putting it into the genitive case.

28.meaning: 'Doubt / uncertainty.' A noun for the wavering state of mind in which one is unsure and cannot settle on what is true — the opposite of firm certainty.
28.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a doubt / some doubt'). The genitive -i is the form taken after a preposition — typically conveying 'in doubt' or 'of doubt.'
28.root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k) — to doubt, be uncertain, waver

29.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
29.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

30.meaning: Causing doubt / disquieting / suspicious. It describes something that unsettles the mind, sowing uncertainty and unease so that one cannot rest assured about it.
30.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word, here 'one that causes doubt') on the mu-...-ī pattern. The final -in ending marks it as indefinite ('a doubt-causing thing') and in the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links it as a description to a preceding indefinite noun.

1.meaning: So to that / for that then — a compound connective: 'so' plus 'to/for' plus the pointing word 'that', gathering up what has been mentioned and directing action toward it.

parts.en: that (pointing to something distant or elevated)

1.grammar: Fa- is 'so/then', drawing a consequence; li- is the preposition 'to/for'. Dhālika is the demonstrative 'that' — the far-pointing form, which in the Qur'an often signals greatness or elevation, not just distance. Demonstratives are fixed words: dhālika keeps this one shape regardless of case.

2.meaning: 'So call upon / so pray' — a command to invoke, supplicate, or call out to someone (especially Allah in prayer), joined by 'so / then'.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) verb with the connector 'fa' ('so / then') prefixed, addressed to a single male 'you'. The verb's root ends in a weak letter, which is dropped in the command form, leaving the short -u sound; the initial vowel of the stem is a helping vowel.

3.meaning: And stand firm / be steadfastly upright — istaqāma means to hold a perfectly straight course without swerving: unwavering uprightness in belief and conduct (the quality asked for in the phrase 'the straight path').
3.grammar: Wa- is 'and'. Istaqim is a command (imperative) addressed to one person: the bare, vowel-less ending (the final -m closed with sukūn, no case vowel) is exactly how Arabic marks a direct command to 'you'. The verb is Form X, a pattern meaning 'to seek/maintain a state' — here, to keep oneself straight and steadfast.

4.meaning: Just as; like; in the same way that. A compound expressing comparison or correspondence between one thing and another.
4.grammar: A compound of the comparison particle ka- ('like / as') with mā ('that which / what'). Together they mean 'just as' or 'in the same way that', introducing a comparison with a following clause. Neither element changes for case; the phrase functions as a connective of likeness.

5.meaning: Means 'you were commanded / you have been ordered' — a past-tense passive verb: an order was given to you by another, the addressee being the one commanded.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The internal vowels u-i mark the passive ('were commanded', not 'commanded'). The -ta ending means 'you' (one male) — the one to whom the command was given.

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: '(You) follow / pursue / take as a path' — a verb meaning to walk after, conform to, and adopt something as one's way, in a form that intensively conveys 'to keep following'.
7.grammar: A present/jussive verb in the reflexive-intensive pattern (iftaʿala). The ta- prefix marks the second-person 'you (one male)'. The silent (vowelless) final consonant is the jussive mood, the form used after negative or conditional particles such as 'do not …' or 'if …'.
7.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

8.meaning: Their desires, inclinations, cravings; the pulls of personal whim and passion — what one leans toward apart from guidance, here belonging to 'them'.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of hawā ('desire, inclination, whim'). The case-vowel -a (accusative) typically marks the object of a verb. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group of males or mixed). Altogether: 'their desires/whims'.
8.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — inclination, desire, whim; to incline toward, to fall

9.meaning: And say / but say — the command 'say!', the word that introduces hundreds of declarations the Prophet is instructed to proclaim; joined by 'and/but' to what precedes.
9.grammar: Wa- is the connector 'and/but'. Qul is the imperative 'say!' addressed to one person: commands end without any case vowel, and here the weak middle letter of the root (the wāw of qāla) drops out, leaving the compact two-letter form. The bare, closed ending is the signature of a direct command.

10.meaning: A first-person singular past-tense verb meaning 'I believed / I have come to faith.' It expresses the act of believing, putting trust and faith in, and affirming as true.
10.grammar: A Form IV past-tense verb ('to have faith, to believe'). The suffix -tu marks a first-person singular subject, 'I.' The whole form is in plain past time: 'I believed / I have believed.'
10.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe/secure; Form IV, to believe, have faith

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
11.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

12.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
12.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: A Book, a scripture — a written record or revealed text. In sacred usage it denotes a divinely revealed Scripture. The indefinite form means 'a book / some scripture' rather than a specific one.
15.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a book') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
15.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; 'kitāb' = something written, a book

16.meaning: And I have been commanded — a past-tense statement in which the speaker reports being ordered or instructed by another; the doer of the commanding is left unnamed, so the focus rests on the speaker as the one under orders.
16.grammar: A past-tense passive verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The inner vowel pattern 'u-i' shows it is passive ('was commanded', no named commander), and the '-tu' ending makes the speaker its subject ('I was commanded').
16.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

17.meaning: So that I may do justice — ʿadala is to be equitable and even-handed, giving each party its due without tilting to either side; with 'so that', it expresses acting for the purpose of fairness.
17.grammar: Li- means 'in order that' and puts the verb in the subjunctive mood: the final -a is the purpose-marking ending ('so that I may…'). The a- prefix marks 'I' as the doer in the imperfect (present) tense.

18.meaning: The spatial or relational interval separating two or more parties: 'in the midst of', 'amongst', or 'in the space between'; joined to the pronoun 'you'.
18.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between/among', fixed in the accusative with an -a, here followed by the attached pronoun -kum ('you', plural). The pronoun is in the genitive position as the object of the adverb, so the whole means 'between/among you'. The final vowel appears as -u (kumu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting vowel.
18.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, that which lies between

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

20.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
20.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

21.meaning: 'And your Lord' — the connector 'and' plus 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer) joined to 'your' (plural). It names Allah as the Lord of the addressed group.
21.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') with a noun carrying the possessive pronoun '-kum' ('your', referring to a group). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate ('[He] is your Lord').
21.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

22.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to us' or 'for us / belonging to us' — combining the preposition 'to/for' with the attached pronoun 'us', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward the speakers.
22.grammar: A preposition fused with an attached pronoun. The base 'li' ('to/for') shifts to 'la' before an attached pronoun, so it appears here with a fatḥa as 'la'; the suffix 'nā' means 'us' (first-person plural). Together it conveys 'for us' — indicating benefit, possession, or direction.

23.meaning: 'Our deeds / our works / our actions' — the plural of 'deed, action, work' joined to 'our'.
23.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached possessive '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('our deeds [are] …').
23.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work; deed, action

24.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'and for you' or 'and you have'. It joins a new statement with 'and', then uses 'for/to you' to express possession or benefit belonging to a group.
24.grammar: Three pieces: wa- ('and') linking to what came before, the preposition la- ('for/to'), and the attached pronoun -kum ('you all', plural). A preposition-plus-'you' phrase like this commonly conveys 'you have' or 'belonging to you'.

25.meaning: 'Your deeds / your works / your actions' — the plural of 'deed, action, work' joined to 'your' (plural).
25.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', referring to a group). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('your deeds [are] …').
25.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work; deed, action

26.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
26.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

27.meaning: Argument / proof — ḥujjah is a case one presses against another: evidence or a plea intended to prevail in a dispute. It can be a valid proof or a hollow contention pressed without right.
27.grammar: The final -a vowel is the accusative case ending — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or after certain particles (e.g. 'there is no…'). It has no tanwīn (-an) here, the shape a noun takes when it is annexed to or negated with what surrounds it. The doubled middle letter reflects the root's sense of pressing a point repeatedly.
27.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — arguing a case, intending, proof

28.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
28.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
28.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

29.meaning: And between you — pointing to the space, relationship, or matter that lies in the middle of two parties.
29.grammar: wa- is the connector 'and'. bayna is a place-word meaning 'between' that always ends in -a because it acts like an adverb of location. -kum means 'you all' (addressing a group); the extra -u at its end is just a helping vowel Arabic adds so the word flows smoothly into the next one — it carries no meaning.

30.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
30.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

31.meaning: He gathers / assembles — a verb meaning to bring together, collect, or unite into one place.
31.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he.' The final -u ending is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of ongoing or future fact.

32.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
32.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
32.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

33.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
33.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

34.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
34.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
34.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They argue, they dispute — an intensive back-and-forth contention in which each side presses its proof against the other.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'mutual action' pattern (Form III), which pictures two parties doing something to each other — here, trading arguments. The yu- prefix marks present tense; the -ūna ending means the subject is 'they' (a group of men or mixed group) and shows the verb is in its plain, statement-making form.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
6.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
6.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: It has been responded to / answered — the call or summons has already received an answer. The passive shape leaves the responders unnamed and puts the spotlight on the fact that the response happened.

parts.en: prefix of the 'seek/receive' verb-pattern, in passive voice

8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb from the pattern that means 'to answer a call' (istajāba). The internal u-ī vowels (ustu-jī-) are the signature of the passive voice: the doer is not named, only that the answering took place. The final -a marks a completed past action with a 'he/it' subject.

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: Their argument, their proof — a ḥujjah is the case or evidence someone puts forward to justify a position.
10.grammar: A feminine noun; the -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or topic of a statement — the thing being talked about. The attached -hum means 'their', belonging to a group.
10.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — argument, proof

11.meaning: Null, refuted, collapsing — literally something that slips and falls; used of an argument that has no footing and is thrown out as worthless.
11.grammar: An active participle (the 'doing' form of the verb: 'that which slips/fails'), made feminine with the -a(t) ending so it can describe a feminine noun. The final -un is nunation, the double vowel that marks an indefinite word ('a...' rather than 'the...') in the nominative case — typically used when the word states what something IS.

12.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
12.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

13.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
13.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

14.meaning: And upon them — combining 'and' with 'on/over/against them'; ʿalā often carries the sense of a burden, obligation, or something coming down on someone.
14.grammar: wa- is 'and'. ʿalā is a preposition ('upon'); before an attached pronoun it takes the shape ʿalay-. The pronoun 'them' is pronounced -him rather than -hum because the preceding ay-sound pulls it toward an i-vowel — a purely phonetic change with no change in meaning.
14.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, being above (source of the sense 'upon, over')

15.meaning: Anger, wrath, indignation — intense displeasure; when ascribed to Allah it denotes His just rejection and condemnation of wrongdoing, free of human passion.
15.grammar: A noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) is the indefinite nominative ending, the case used for the subject of a sentence ('[some] wrath …'), and the tanwīn marks it as indefinite ('a/an').

16.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to a phrase 'for them' or 'they have' — literally 'and to/for them', expressing that something belongs to or is owed to a group.
16.grammar: Two prefixes on a pronoun: wa- means 'and', and the preposition la- means 'for/to'. The pronoun -hum means 'them', a group of males or a mixed group. The preposition la- attached to a pronoun commonly conveys possession or entitlement — 'they have' or 'for them (belongs) …'.

17.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

18.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty in force. Describes something powerful and unrelenting in its strength or rigor.
18.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting a firmly established quality (intensity, severity). The final -un ending combines the nominative case (used for the subject or a predicate describing who/what something is) with nunation (the -n sound), which marks the word as indefinite, i.e. 'a severe one' rather than 'the severe one'.
18.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun, masculine singular, meaning 'who / which / the one that.' It links a following clause to a noun, marking it out as 'the [noun] that…'
2.grammar: A masculine-singular relative pronoun. It is indeclinable (its form does not change for case) and introduces a description, equivalent to 'the one who/which…'

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
3.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

4.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

5.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
5.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

6.meaning: 'And the balance / the scales' — the instrument for weighing, and by extension the principle of just weight and equilibrium.
6.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb. The mīzān pattern (mifʿāl) denotes an instrument — here a thing used for weighing.

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
7.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

8.meaning: (What) will make you know / let you perceive — a causative verb: to cause someone to be aware of something otherwise hidden from them.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative pattern (Form IV): the plain verb darā means 'to know/perceive', so yudrī means 'he/it makes (someone) know'. The yu- prefix signals present tense with a 'he/it' subject; the attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one person) — the person being made to know.

9.meaning: A particle of hope and expectation, roughly "perhaps / it may be that / in the hope that." It presents what follows as a hoped-for or anticipated outcome rather than a certainty — often introducing the wisdom or possible result behind a command.
9.grammar: A particle, not a verb or noun, so it has no tense or case of its own. Like inna, it attaches to a following noun or pronoun and puts it in the accusative case, then the rest of the clause states the hoped-for outcome.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — most particularly the Last Hour, the appointed time of the world's end and the Resurrection; literally a portion of time, an hour, or a moment.
10.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its l assimilates into the following 'sun letter' s, hence the doubled s). The -a ending is the accusative case, the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb or by what follows certain particles.
10.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a span of time, an hour; the appointed Hour

11.meaning: Near, close, at hand — close in distance, time, or relationship; readily accessible.
11.grammar: A singular masculine adjective on the intensive paradigm faʿīl, meaning 'near/close'. The ending -un (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('near') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate describing a subject.

1.meaning: To seek to hasten something, to want it brought about quickly, to demand it be rushed or sped up.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb of the 'seeking' (form X) pattern, 'to want [something] hurried, to ask that it be hastened.' The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain ongoing or habitual action ('he seeks to hasten it').

2.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
2.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
5.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

6.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
6.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

7.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
7.root: — (relative pronoun)

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
8.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

9.meaning: An active participle meaning 'those who are apprehensive / fearful / full of awe and dread.' It describes people in a state of anxious, reverent fear — wary and on edge out of awe or concern over an outcome.
9.grammar: An active participle (a describing word naming the doer of an action/state) in the masculine plural, 'ones who are apprehensive.' It follows the mufʿil pattern (mu- + i-vowelled stem, mushfiq), the active participle of a form IV verb (ashfaqa). The -ūna ending marks masculine plural and the nominative case, the base case used for a subject or a descriptive predicate.
9.root: ش-ف-ق (sh-f-q) — to be apprehensive, fearful out of care or awe

10.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
10.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

11.meaning: And they know — knowledge held as settled awareness, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
11.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a present-tense verb; the stem yaʿlam- carries no ending vowel of its own — the written u-vowel belongs to the -ūna ending, which tells you the subject is 'they' (a group) and that the verb is in its plain indicative (statement) form, describing what they actually, presently do.

12.meaning: that it / that she — a connector meaning 'that...,' introducing a reported fact or content clause, with an attached feminine 'it/she' as its subject. The base particle gives certainty and emphasis to the clause it opens.
12.grammar: An emphasizing particle meaning 'that...,' used to introduce a statement of fact (as in 'they know that...'). It grammatically governs a following noun in the accusative; here that noun is the attached pronoun -hā, 'it/she' (feminine), serving as the subject of the 'that'-clause.

13.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
13.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
13.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

14.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
14.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

15.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
15.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

16.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
16.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

17.meaning: They dispute, they wrangle in doubt — persistent quarrelling that springs from and feeds scepticism, arguing for argument's sake rather than to reach truth.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'mutual action' pattern (Form III), picturing parties trading doubts and objections with each other. The yu- prefix marks present tense; the -ūna ending marks a plural 'they' subject in the plain statement form of the verb.

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

19.meaning: The Hour — the appointed final time: the moment of the world's ending and the Resurrection. Though literally 'an hour' (a span of time), with the definite article it denotes that singular, decisive coming Hour.
19.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 's' (heard as 'as-sāʿa'). The final -i is genitive — the case used when the word is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the Hour') or follows a preposition.
19.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a passing moment or span of time; an 'hour'

20.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'surely in / indeed within'. It joins an emphasis particle ('surely, indeed') with the preposition 'in', stressing that something is firmly located or contained inside.
20.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, indeed') used to strengthen a statement. fī is a preposition ('in/within') and, like all prepositions, governs a following noun, putting it into the genitive case.

21.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
21.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
21.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

22.meaning: Far, distant, or remote — in space, time, or figuratively (as in being far from the truth or from guidance).
22.grammar: An adjective in the intensive/quality paradigm. The -in ending marks the genitive case with indefiniteness ('a far …'); the genitive usually links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: Subtle, Most Kind — laṭīf combines fineness and gentleness: One whose kindness reaches people in imperceptible ways and whose knowledge penetrates the finest hidden things. One of the beautiful names of Allah.
2.grammar: An intensive adjective pattern (faʿīl) expressing a permanent quality. The final -un is nunation in the nominative case: it typically marks the word as a predicate — stating what someone IS ('...is Subtle').

3.meaning: Means 'with/over His servants' — concerning the worshippers and bondservants who belong to Allah. 'ʿibad' are those who serve and submit; the pronoun makes them 'His.'
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/of/concerning') joined to the plural noun 'ʿibad' with the possessive -hi ('His'). The -i vowel reflects the genitive state required after the preposition. The word denotes those who serve and worship, here belonging to Allah.

4.meaning: 'He provides / grants sustenance'. It denotes the act of providing the means of life — food, wealth, and every blessing — bestowed by a giver upon recipients. Present tense, third person masculine singular.
4.grammar: The 'ya-' prefix marks a present/ongoing action by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, used for plain statements of fact about an ongoing or habitual action.
4.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to sustain, provision

5.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
5.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

6.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
6.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
6.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

7.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
7.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

8.meaning: The Strong / the All-Powerful. It describes one possessing full and unfailing strength and might, with power that never weakens — when used of Allah, the One whose strength is absolute.
8.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') plus an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern meaning 'strong, mighty' (conveying strength as a deep, constant quality). The final -u ending marks the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a noun being identified.

9.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
9.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
3.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
3.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

4.meaning: A tilled field, crop, or harvest — cultivated land and what is sown and grown in it; tillage.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the second term in a possessive pairing.
4.root: ح-ر-ث (ḥ-r-th) — to till, plough, cultivate; sowing and tillage

5.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
5.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
5.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

6.meaning: We increase — to give someone more, to add to what they have. With 'We' as speaker it expresses Allah speaking in the majestic plural.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb whose na- prefix means 'we'. It ends with no vowel at all (zid, not zidu) — this clipped 'jussive' form is the shape a verb takes after words like 'whoever...' or 'if...', marking it as the result half of a condition ('whoever does X, We increase...').

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: His tillage / his harvest — ḥarth is cultivation: the field a person sows and works, and by extension the yield he hopes to reap; often used figuratively for what one labours toward.
9.grammar: The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or when the word means '...OF something'. The attached -hi means 'his'; it is pronounced -hi rather than -hu because the i-vowel before it pulls it into harmony — same meaning either way.

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
10.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

12.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
12.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
12.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

13.meaning: A tilled field, crop, or harvest — cultivated land and what is sown and grown in it; tillage.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the second term in a possessive pairing.
13.root: ح-ر-ث (ḥ-r-th) — to till, plough, cultivate; sowing and tillage

14.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
14.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
14.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

15.meaning: 'We give him / We grant him' — the bestowing or granting of something, done by 'we', directed to a single male recipient.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb (causative form with the nu- prefix marking 'we') plus the attached object pronoun -hi ('him'). The verb's weak final letter is dropped in the jussive (majzūm) mood used after conditional particles, so it reads 'we (will) give him' as the answer to a condition.
15.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

16.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
16.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

17.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
17.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

18.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
18.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
19.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

20.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
20.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
20.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
