Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: Lowliness, humbleness, gentle submission — the state of making oneself low and meek out of tender care, the opposite of pride and harshness.
6.grammar: A noun ('humility') carrying 'the' (al-, here the l assimilates into the following dh). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in a '… OF …' possessive relationship, or follows a preposition.
6.root: ذ-ل-ل (dh-l-l) — to be lowly, humble, submissive, abased

7.meaning: They look toward, watch for, or await; a present-tense act of a group either gazing at something or expecting/waiting for it to happen.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). The full -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action that is happening or habitual.
7.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, watch, await

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: The eye or its glance — a single look, especially the quick movement or blink of the eyelid; by extension, the briefest flicker of vision.
9.grammar: A simple singular noun. The -in ending combines the genitive -i, which a word takes after a preposition or when it stands as the second half of an 'X of Y' phrase, with nunation (-n) marking indefiniteness: 'a glance' rather than 'the glance'.

10.meaning: Hidden, furtive, stealthy — kept low and concealed, as a look stolen secretly out of fear or shame. From the root 'to be hidden'.
10.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern ('thoroughly hidden'). Adjectives copy the case of the noun they describe, so the -in ending shows it is describing an indefinite genitive noun: the -i is the genitive case (after a preposition or in an 'of' phrase) and the -n (nunation) marks indefiniteness.
10.root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden, concealed

11.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
11.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: They believed, they came to faith; to place trust and security in something and affirm it as true (the inner act of faith).
13.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form IV (causative) pattern. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for a completed action ('they believed'). The final written alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

14.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
14.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

15.meaning: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
15.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
15.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

16.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
16.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

17.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
17.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
17.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

18.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
18.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

19.meaning: And their families — wa-ahlīhim means 'and their families/households', referring to those saved along with the believers on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: their (third person masculine plural possessive suffix)

19.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Ahl is a noun meaning family, household, or companions, in the genitive after a preceding verb or as an object. The suffix -him is third-person masculine plural possessive. Context: the wrongdoers will be told on Judgment Day of their loss — themselves and their families.
19.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, people, those who belong to

20.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
20.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
20.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

21.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
21.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

22.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
22.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

23.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
23.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

24.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
24.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

25.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
25.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

26.meaning: A punishment / torment — painful chastisement or suffering imposed as a penalty. The word names the punishment itself, stated indefinitely ('a punishment').
26.grammar: A noun, 'punishment/torment'. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and genitive in case — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a punishment').

27.meaning: Lasting, abiding, permanent — that which stays and does not pass away. It is the active participle of Form IV aqāma, 'to make stay, establish', so literally 'remaining / made to endure'.
27.grammar: An active participle: the mu- prefix turns the verb into 'the one who / that which does it', here 'that which abides'. The -in ending is the genitive -i (taken after a preposition or as the second word of an 'X of Y' phrase, or agreeing with such a noun) plus nunation (-n) for indefiniteness.
27.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, remain, be established

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

6.meaning: They will help them — the present/imperfect verb of naṣara with an attached object pronoun -nahum ('them'); third person masculine plural.
6.grammar: A Form I present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural; the -ūna ending is indicative. The object pronoun -hum (masculine plural) indicates 'them' as the recipients of the help. Together yanṣurūnahum means 'they help them'.
6.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, give victory; yanṣurūnahum means 'they support them'

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
8.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
8.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
10.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
13.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

14.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
14.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: A way, road, or path — a route one travels; by extension a course, means, or manner of proceeding.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -in ending (tanwīn 'i') marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness ('a way'). The genitive typically appears after a preposition or as the second noun in a possessive link ('… of a way'/'a way of …').

1.meaning: Respond! Answer! Comply! A plural command from a Form X verb meaning 'to answer a call, to respond favorably, to grant a request.' It calls on a group to give a positive, obedient response.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb, Form X, addressed to a plural 'you all.' It begins with the connecting (helping) alif pronounced when starting speech. The -ū ending directs the order to a group of males (or mixed group): 'all of you, respond!'

2.meaning: 'To your Lord.' Rabb is richer than 'lord': the Master who owns, sustains, nurtures, and brings His creatures step by step to their completeness — care and authority combined. With li- it means 'to/for your Rabb'.
2.grammar: Preposition + noun + pronoun. li- ('to/for') forces the genitive case, so rabb takes the -i ending — the case a noun always takes after a preposition or when something is 'of' it. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' addressed to a group ('you all').

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
4.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: He/it comes, brings, or arrives — to come or to bring (something) about. The form points to an action not yet completed (present or future).
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'). The ya- prefix (a single, undoubled yāʾ) marks a single male/thing subject. The final -a (in -iya) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', giving the sense '… that he come' or '… until he comes'.

7.meaning: 'a day' — a period of daylight, a single day, or more broadly an appointed time or epoch. It can refer to an ordinary day or to a momentous, decisive day.
7.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('a day'): the doubled-n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

8.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
8.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'a turning back, a repelling, a reversal' — the act or possibility of something being averted or sent back; also 'no averting it' when negated.
9.grammar: A verbal noun of place/action (the ma- prefix forms such nouns) meaning 'a turning back / averting.' The final -a ending is accusative; this is the form a noun takes as a direct object, and notably the form used after the absolute negation particle ('there is no … at all').

10.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
10.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: A refuge, shelter, place to flee to for protection — literally 'a place of taking refuge', from the verb 'to resort to, seek shelter'.
16.grammar: A noun of place: the ma- prefix on a root builds 'the place where the action happens', so malja' = 'place of refuge'. The -in ending joins the genitive -i (used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship, often after 'min' — 'any refuge') with nunation (-n) marking it indefinite: 'a refuge', any refuge at all.
16.root: ل-ج-أ (l-j-ʾ) — to take refuge, resort to

17.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
17.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

18.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
18.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

19.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
19.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

20.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
20.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

21.meaning: Denial, protest, repudiation — the power to reject or disown what happens to you, or to raise any objection against it. From the root 'to deny, refuse to recognize'.
21.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern serving as a verbal noun: 'denying, protesting'. The -in ending is the genitive -i — the case taken after a preposition such as min ('any…of') or as the second term of an 'X of Y' phrase — plus nunation (-n) showing indefiniteness: 'any denial at all'.
21.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to deny, refuse to recognize

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: they turn away / they move away. Refers to the dignified act of distancing oneself from something unworthy — walking away rather than engaging.

parts.en: they turned away, they moved away (Form IV, past 3rd plural)

2.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine plural, Form IV (aʿraḍa — to turn away, to disregard). The -ū ending marks the plural.
2.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth; Form IV: to turn away, to show one's broadside (i.e., to ignore)

3.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'so/then what…'. It joins the connector 'so/then' with mā, a word that can ask 'what?' or function in exclamation ('how…!'), often expressing wonder or amazement.
3.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle ('so/then'). mā is an unchanging particle/pronoun used for questions ('what?') or exclamations ('how…!'); it has no case ending and stays the same in every position.

4.meaning: 'We sent you / We dispatched you' — the act of sending forth one male addressee, as one is sent on a mission or as a messenger.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to send), with two attached pronouns: 'nā' is the subject 'we,' and the final 'ka' is the object 'you' (one male). So it states a completed act, 'we sent you.'

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
5.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
5.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: A guardian, keeper, ever-watchful custodian — one charged with preserving, protecting, and keeping careful watch. The intensive pattern implies constant, thorough guarding.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern: not just one who guards once, but one whose nature is to guard. The -an ending is the accusative case with nunation: accusative typically marks the object of a verb or a state/capacity — 'as a guardian' — and the -n shows the word is indefinite.

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: The conveying / the delivering (of a message): the act of passing on and communicating something so it reaches its hearers fully and clearly; a verbal noun naming that act.
10.grammar: A definite verbal noun (a noun naming an action) with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('… is …').
10.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to arrive at; to convey

11.meaning: 'And indeed we…' — the connector 'and' (wa) joined to the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') with an attached 'we'. It links to what precedes and strongly asserts a statement about the group.
11.grammar: A connective 'and' (wa-) plus the emphasis particle inna, with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'we'). inna strongly affirms the nominal statement that follows; -nā is its ism. The nūn of the pronoun -nā merges in writing with the doubled n of inna (so only the alif is written after the shaddah), but it is phonologically part of the pronoun, giving wa-innā ('and indeed we …').

12.meaning: 'when / whenever' — a particle pointing to a time, usually a future or expected occasion ('at the time that ...').
12.grammar: A time particle ('when, whenever') that introduces a clause and points to the moment something happens, typically expected or recurring. It sets up a 'when X, then Y' relationship and does not itself alter word endings.

13.meaning: 'We made (someone) taste / We caused to experience' — to let a person undergo or feel something (often a hardship or a favor), spoken in the first-person plural.
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) causative verb (form IV — 'to make taste'). The suffix -nā marks the first-person plural ('we') as the doers and indicates a completed action. The causative form turns 'to taste' into 'to make someone taste / cause to experience'.
13.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience, to feel

14.meaning: the human being, mankind — the human creature in general, marked by sociability and forgetfulness.
14.grammar: A noun for the human being, with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the direct object of a verb or following certain particles. Used generically, it denotes humankind as a type.
14.root: أ-ن-س ('-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humanness

15.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
15.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
15.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

16.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
16.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.

17.meaning: He rejoiced / was glad: an experience of joy, gladness, and elation; the bare form expresses one masculine doer's delight.
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular ('he …'). The final -a is the standard ending of the basic completed-action verb, indicating one masculine doer and finished action ('he rejoiced'). It reads only as this perfect form; the corresponding command 'rejoice!' is a distinct word (ifraḥ), not a re-voweling of this one.
17.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — to rejoice, be glad, exult

18.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
18.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
19.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

20.meaning: Verb meaning 'it strikes / befalls / hits (them)' — to reach and affect someone, said of anything that lands upon a person, whether benefit or harm.

parts.en: strike, befall, hit the mark (hollow-verb stem)

20.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb of the hollow root ص-و-ب, with a feminine third-person subject ('she/it'), here in the jussive mood — the shortened form (note the bare '-ṣib' without a final vowel, the long vowel of the stem dropped) used after conditional particles ('if … strikes them') and certain other particles. The 'tu-' prefix is simply the Form I imperfect prefix for a feminine subject, not a Form IV marker. The attached '-hum' is the object 'them.'
20.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, strike correctly; to befall or reach

21.meaning: "A bad thing / an evil / a misfortune" — something evil, harmful, or unpleasant; a misdeed or a piece of bad fortune.
21.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective. The -at ending marks it feminine; the final -un is nominative case with tanwīn (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a bad thing'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence. It is the counterpart of ḥasana.
21.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, to be bad

22.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
22.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

23.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she/it put forward / sent ahead / advanced beforehand' — to send something on ahead, often used of deeds a person has done in advance and dispatched before themselves.
23.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter) that conveys deliberately putting something forward. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it sent ahead'.
23.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — coming before, advancing, putting forward

24.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
24.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

25.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
25.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

26.meaning: the human being, mankind — the human creature in general, marked by sociability and forgetfulness.
26.grammar: A noun for the human being, with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the direct object of a verb or following certain particles. Used generically, it denotes humankind as a type.
26.root: أ-ن-س ('-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humanness

27.meaning: Deeply ungrateful — one who actively denies and is thankless for blessings received. The intensive form stresses a persistent, ingrained ingratitude (and, of the same root, denial of faith).
27.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿūl pattern), marking a strong, habitual trait — 'profoundly ungrateful.' The -un (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ('a…') and nominative, the case used for a subject or a predicate that describes it.
27.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over; to be ungrateful, to disbelieve

1.meaning: A combination 'to/for Allah / belonging to Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the name Allah, expressing that something is due to, owned by, or directed toward Allah.
1.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'to / for / belonging to'. 'Allah' follows, with the initial alif of 'Allāh' elided after li-. The final -i is the genitive ending required after a preposition; it marks Allah as the One to whom something belongs or is directed.

2.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he creates / he brings into being'. It denotes originating and forming something, bringing it into existence — an act distinctively ascribed to Allah.
5.grammar: A present/future verb (Form I, khalaqa, 'to create'). The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is indicative, expressing a plain statement of present or ongoing/repeated action (as opposed to subjunctive or jussive forms).
5.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape, measure out

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

8.meaning: 'He gives freely, bestows' — wahaba is to grant as a pure gift, with no payment or claim in return; the divine Name al-Wahhāb ('the ever-Bestowing') comes from this same root.

parts.en: give freely, bestow as a gift

8.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: ya- means 'he'. The root's first letter (w) drops out in the present tense, a regular feature of w-initial verbs, leaving yahabu. The final -u is the indicative mood ending, marking an ordinary factual statement — 'he gives / keeps giving' — rather than a wish or condition.

9.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
9.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

10.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

11.meaning: Females / female beings. The plural of 'female', denoting things or beings of the feminine sex.
11.grammar: A plural noun ('females'). The -an ending (tanwīn with fatḥa) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('they call upon … females').
11.root: أ-ن-ث (ʾ-n-th) — to be female, the female sex

12.meaning: 'And He gives freely' — the same verb of pure, unearned giving, joined by 'and' to a parallel act of bestowal.

parts.en: give freely, bestow as a gift

12.grammar: wa- ('and') plus a present-tense verb: ya- marks 'he', the stem -hab- is 'bestow' (the root's initial w regularly disappears in the present), and the final -u is the indicative mood — a straightforward statement of ongoing fact, 'and he gives'.

13.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

14.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
14.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

15.meaning: 'The males' — dhukūr is a plural of dhakar, 'a male'; with the definite article, males as a class.
15.grammar: Definite plural noun. al- is 'the' (its l assimilates in sound to the following dh, heard as adh-dh…). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb — the thing given, made, or acted upon. Being definite, it takes no nunation (-n).

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: 'He pairs them / makes them into couples' — Form II of the root 'pair, spouse': to join together in pairs, to give both kinds together or couple one thing with another.
2.grammar: Present-tense Form II verb with an object pronoun. yu- marks 'he' (the u-vowel is characteristic of Form II); the doubled middle letter of zawwij gives the causative sense 'make into pairs'. The -u before the pronoun is the indicative mood, a plain statement; -hum is the attached pronoun 'them', the direct object.

3.meaning: 'Males' — dhukrān, another plural of dhakar ('male'), used for male offspring or male individuals as a group.
3.grammar: An indefinite plural noun. The -an ending is the accusative case with nunation: accusative is the case of a verb's direct object (the ones given or made), and the -n marks indefiniteness — 'males' in general, not 'the males'.

4.meaning: 'And females' — ināth is the plural of unthā, 'a female'; with wa-, 'and females' as a class or as female offspring.
4.grammar: wa- ('and') joining an indefinite plural noun. The -an ending combines the accusative case — the ending of a direct object, the thing given or made — with nunation (-n), which signals indefiniteness: 'females', unspecified.

5.meaning: and He places / sets / appoints — a verb meaning to put or set something somewhere, to make or render a thing into a certain state, to appoint.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a joining wa- ('and') in front. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain ongoing or future statement: 'and he places / will set / appoints'.
5.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to place, set, make, render, appoint

6.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
6.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

8.meaning: Barren, sterile — incapable of bearing offspring; the faʿīl pattern makes it a fixed quality, 'utterly without issue'. Used of a person, and figuratively of anything fruitless.
8.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern denoting a settled characteristic. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation: the accusative case marks a direct object or a predicate/state ('makes … barren', 'as barren'), and the -n shows the word is indefinite.

9.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
9.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

10.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
10.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').
10.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

11.meaning: 'All-Powerful,' 'fully able,' 'one who has complete power and capability.' An intensive form expressing that the one described possesses perfect, unrestricted power to do whatever is willed — a quality applied supremely to Allah.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, established capability. The '-un' ending (tanwīn al-ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the 'subject/predicate' case) together with indefiniteness — typically the role of a subject or, very often, a predicate describing who or what something is.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'a human being / a mortal' — a person of flesh, mankind as physical, mortal creatures, as opposed to the divine. The indefinite form means 'a human'.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun preceded by the preposition li- ('for / belonging to'). The ending -in (nunation with 'i') marks the genitive case and indefiniteness, as required after the preposition; the noun is grammatically singular but refers to humankind collectively.
3.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — skin, outward form; human being, mortal

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: 'That He should speak to him' — Form II kallama means to address someone directly, to speak to. With its attached pronoun: to speak to him.
5.grammar: Present-tense Form II verb: yu- marks 'he', and the doubled middle letter of kallim makes the root 'word/speech' into 'address someone with speech'. The -a before the pronoun is the subjunctive mood ending, which a verb takes after particles like an ('that'): it frames the act as possibility — 'that he should speak' — not plain fact. -hu is 'him', the person addressed.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: Waḥy: revelation — a swift, subtle, secret communication cast directly into the heart or mind. The word covers divine inspiration in all its quiet immediacy, communication without ordinary speech.
8.grammar: A verbal noun ('the act of revealing'). The -an ending is the accusative case with nunation: the accusative here typically expresses manner or means — '(by way of) revelation' — a common use of the case beyond marking direct objects; the -n marks indefiniteness.
8.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to inspire, communicate swiftly and secretly

9.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
9.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
10.root: — (preposition)

11.meaning: 'Behind, beyond' — warāʾ denotes what lies on the far side of something, out of sight behind it (and can even mean 'beyond' in either direction). The initial wa- is part of the word itself, not 'and'.
11.grammar: A noun of location used like a preposition. Its final -i is the genitive case: the ending a word takes after a preposition (such as min, 'from') or when it stands in an 'X of Y' chain — 'from behind (of) something'. The hamza is the word's own final root letter, here written on a yā'-shaped seat.

12.meaning: A veil, screen, barrier — anything that stands between two things and blocks sight or access. From the root 'to screen off'; a ḥijāb is the partition itself, whatever conceals one side from the other.
12.grammar: A simple noun on the fiʿāl pattern. The -in ending pairs the genitive case -i — taken after a preposition or as the second half of an 'X of Y' phrase ('from behind a veil') — with nunation (-n), which marks the noun as indefinite: 'a veil', unspecified.

13.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
13.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

14.meaning: '(That) He should send / dispatch / let loose.' To send forth a messenger, a wind, a punishment, or the like.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb of the form IV (causative) pattern, 'to send, to let loose.' The yu- prefix marks the doer as 'he.' The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after particles meaning 'that / so that' and signals an intended or hypothetical action rather than a plain statement.
14.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; messengers, being sent forth

15.meaning: "a messenger / an envoy" — one who is sent bearing a message; 'rasūl' is an emissary commissioned to convey something on behalf of the one who sent him, especially a prophet sent with a divine message.
15.grammar: A masculine noun on the faʿūl pattern, indefinite ('a messenger'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form used for the direct object of a verb; the written alif carries this ending.
15.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, messenger

16.meaning: "So that He reveals" — to send waḥy, the swift, subtle communication by which Allah conveys His message to a chosen servant, often through inspiration or via an angel, rather than by ordinary speech.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ("he"), in Form IV — the causative pattern (yu- prefix with an -i- stem vowel) whose sense in this verb is to cause revelation to reach someone. The fa- prefix means "so/then", tying the action to what came before it as a result or continuation. The verb is in the subjunctive mood, used after particles of purpose or result: on this weak-final verb the mood shows as a final -a vowel on the last root letter (y), giving yūḥiya — "so that he may reveal" — in place of the plain-statement form yūḥī.
16.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — swift, secret communication; divine revelation

17.meaning: 'By His permission / with His leave'. It joins 'with/by' to the noun 'permission, leave, sanction' and an attached pronoun 'His', indicating something done by the authorization of the one referred to.
17.grammar: The prefix 'bi-' is a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by (means of)'. It places the following noun in the genitive case, shown by the '-i' ending. The attached '-hi' is a possessive pronoun, 'His' (or 'its'), so the whole reads 'by His permission'.
17.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; to hear/heed

18.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
18.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

19.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
19.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
19.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

20.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
20.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

21.meaning: "Most High, Exalted" — an intensive adjective describing one who is supremely elevated above all else in rank, majesty, and being; as a divine attribute it is al-ʿAliyy, the One utterly transcendent above creation.
21.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, meaning not merely "high" but "supremely high by very nature". The -un ending does two things: the -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence or for a description stated about the subject ("X is Most High"); the final -n (tanwīn) marks the word as grammatically indefinite in form — the normal state of an adjective used as a predicate, even when it describes One who is unique.

22.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
22.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
22.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: 'We revealed / inspired' — the act of God conveying revelation or inspiration; to communicate a message swiftly and privately into someone's heart or to a prophet. Here attributed to 'we'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern (to convey/send down a revelation). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we revealed'. As past tense, it reports a completed act.
2.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, to inspire, to convey swiftly and secretly

3.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
3.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

4.meaning: "A spirit / an inspiration" — rūḥ is the life-giving breath or spirit; the Qur'an also uses it for the revelation itself, because just as the spirit gives life to the body, revelation gives life to hearts. It can likewise name the angel of revelation.
4.grammar: A singular noun. The -an ending is the accusative, indefinite: the -a marks the accusative case, which typically flags the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon, e.g. what is sent or given), and the -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite — "a spirit / an inspiration", not "the spirit".
4.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — spirit, breath, wind; ease and life

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: Our affair, matter, command, or concern — that which we are dealing with or commanded to do. 'Amr' spans both a 'matter/situation' and a 'command/order'.
6.grammar: A noun ('affair') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition ('… of our affair' / 'in our affair'). The attached -nā means 'our'.
6.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also 'matter, affair, situation'

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

9.meaning: knows / is aware

parts.en: it knows / you know (imperfect verb, feminine)

9.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form I (دَرَى), 3rd person feminine singular or 2nd person feminine singular, indicative; in construction with مَا (what) meaning 'knows not what'
9.root: د-ر-ي (d-r-y) — to know, to be aware of

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written, recorded text. Built on the idea of writing and committing to record, it denotes an authoritative written revelation collected and set down.
11.grammar: A definite masculine singular noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (the 'what it is'). The prefixed al- makes it definite: 'the Book' rather than 'a book'.

12.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: the faith
13.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

14.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
14.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

15.meaning: 'We made him / appointed him / rendered him so.' The verb of making or setting into a state (jaʿala), with attached pronouns for the subject 'we' and the object 'him.'
15.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject ending -nā ('we,' a completed act by a plural or majestic 'we') and the attached object -hu ('him/it'). It denotes making, placing, or rendering the object into some state.
15.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

16.meaning: 'A light' — light, radiance, or illumination; that by which things become visible. Often used figuratively for guidance, clarity, and spiritual illumination.
16.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a light').

17.meaning: "We guide" — the act of hidāya: showing the way, directing someone to the right path and enabling them to reach it. With the divine "We", it expresses Allah's granting of guidance.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means "we" — first person plural, which in the Qur'an is often the majestic "We" of Allah. The shadda (doubling sign) on this nūn reflects Qur'anic recitation: when a word ending in the sound n is followed by a word beginning with n, the two merge into one doubled nūn (idghām), and the script writes that doubling on the verb itself. The verb's third root letter is weak (y), so the word ends in the long vowel -ī, which belongs to the stem itself; on such weak-ending verbs the usual -u of a plain statement is not pronounced, so the long -ī simply marks the ordinary present indicative: "We guide" as a standing fact.
17.root: هـ-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance; showing the right way

18.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
18.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

19.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
19.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

20.meaning: 'We will / We wish' — to will, want, or choose for something to be; expresses volition.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb. The prefix means 'we'; the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative ('we will / we wish'). Its nūn carries a shadda (doubling) because the preceding connector 'man' ('whoever') merges into it, so it is sounded '-nn-'.
20.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
21.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

22.meaning: 'Servants / slaves of …' — devoted worshippers who belong wholly to their Master. The word denotes those in willing servitude to Allah, here joined to a possessor.
22.grammar: عِبَاد ('ʿibād') is the plural of 'servant/slave.' The -i ending is the genitive case, which links the word to what follows in an 'of …' relationship — here completed by the attached pronoun نَا ('-nā', 'our'), giving 'servants of ours / Our servants.'
22.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a devoted slave

23.meaning: "and indeed you / and truly you" — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') joined to the 'you' pronoun, strongly affirming a statement about the person addressed.
23.grammar: An emphatic opening particle (inna) with an attached pronoun. Inna asserts and strengthens the sentence ('it is certainly the case that…') and grammatically takes its noun/pronoun in the accusative; the attached -ka ('you') is that accusative pronoun. The leading wa- is 'and'.

24.meaning: "You surely guide" — the same act of guiding to the right path, addressed to a "you", and strengthened by an emphatic particle: truly, certainly you guide.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb with two prefixes. The la- is the emphatic lām: it adds certainty and force — "surely, indeed". The ta- prefix marks the second person: "you (masculine singular)". The verb ends in the long -ī of its weak third root letter (y); on such verbs the indicative -u of a plain statement is not pronounced, so the -ī itself carries the ordinary present-tense sense: "you do guide" as an affirmed, ongoing reality.
24.root: هـ-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance; showing the right way

25.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
25.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

26.meaning: 'A path / road / way' — a route one travels; frequently used in a moral or spiritual sense for a way of life or course of conduct.
26.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The -in ending (the genitive with 'tanwīn') marks it as 'a path' (no 'the') and signals the genitive case — the case used after prepositions or when a noun is linked to a following noun. It often corresponds to English 'to/of a path'.

27.meaning: 'Straight / upright / undeviating' — describing something that runs true without bending or wandering; applied to a 'path' it means a direct, correct way that leads soundly to its goal.
27.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'straight/upright') from a verb meaning 'to be/become straight'. It is indefinite, and the -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn'. As a describing word it normally follows and agrees with the noun it modifies, matching that noun in being indefinite and in the genitive case.

1.meaning: A path, road, or way. It is frequently used for a clear, broad highway, and figuratively for the straight way of right guidance and conduct.
1.grammar: A masculine noun in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending. The genitive typically means the word is linked to a following noun ('the path OF …') or follows a preposition.

2.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
2.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

3.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
4.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
7.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
7.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
10.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
10.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

11.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
11.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

12.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
12.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: "Comes to / ends up at" — from ṣāra, "to become, to arrive at a final state or destination". It describes things moving toward and finally reaching their end point — the destination in which matters ultimately settle.

parts.en: come to, end up at, become

14.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix here marks the subject: it is the form used both for "she/it" (with a feminine subject, such as a plural of things) and for "you (masculine singular)" — context decides which. The middle weak root letter appears as the long -ī- of the stem. The final -u is the indicative ending: it marks a plain statement of fact in the present/future — "does come to, will end up at" — as opposed to the -a of the subjunctive or a dropped vowel after certain particles.
14.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become; to reach an end state or destination

15.meaning: The matters, affairs, or things; the plural of "affair/matter," denoting all the various businesses, situations, or commands taken together.
15.grammar: A definite plural noun with prefixed al- ("the"), the plural of the word for "matter/affair." The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as the doer/topic of an action.
